learning_outcomes.text: Provide knowledge and skills in the field of experimentation, measurement and testing on machines, structures and products and industrial processes.
Understand the meaning of measurement, experimentation and testing.
Understand sensors, main physical principles used and measuring chains for different types of measurement.
Understand data analysis and processing, taking into account measurement errors and uncertainties.
Identify the most suitable methods for carrying out experimentation or control on a product / structure / machinery and to assess / verify / test its characteristics.

Understand how performance can be verified and systems can be improved, innovating the systems also through the development and improvement of measurement and control methods, in the field of mechanical engineering.

Achieve an adequate preparation to access the third level of university studies (attendance at second level master and doctoral schools), in order to further deepen knowledge and skills in the field of research.

syllabus_topics: Measurement chains and sensors
Concept of measurement
Errors, classification and propagation in the measurement chains
Data processing, mean and variance
Digital sampling
Power spectra
Autocorrelation of signals
Analog and digital filters
Basic measures and concepts of performance verification and testing
Measurement systems and main components, connections and measuring chain
Characteristics of the instruments
Constant and variable signals over time
Errors; errors definition, identification and propagation in the measurement chain
Temperature measurements; seebek effect and thermocouples, thermocouple laws, thermoresistance and thermistors
Advanced temperature measurements; radiometric systems and errors
Concepts of noise, physical principles and Acoustics and noise Measurements
Flow measurements; basic principles and throttling systems
Basics of pressure probes - Pitot, COBRA probes and directional systems
Advanced pressure measurements (socket geometries, errors, problems) 2D and 3D pneumatic probes and construction techniques, characterization, data reduction
Introduction to LabVIEW - Computer-aided acquisition systems
Basics of electric strain gauges, torque measurements with strain gauge systems
Dynamic sensors, sensor characterization
Principles of non-intrusive measures; PIV systems, operating principle
Principles measurements with LDV systems
Non destructive testing
Ultrasonic techniques
Testing

assessment_methods.method: Measurement experience in the laboratory with related report (voluntary, in groups)

assessment_rules: The final oral examination is divided into a presentation and discussion of an optional lab report (ten-fifteen minutes) and a standard oral exam (25-30 minutes) with two theoretical questions or an application question. The total duration of the oral exam is about 30-40 minutes. Grading ranges from 18-22 for sufficient knowledge to 29-30 and Honors (Lode) for excellent and outstanding understanding, critical thinking, and originality.
